courses.name: Computational Methods
courses.description: Basic computational methods for interpolation, least squares, approximation, numerical quadrature, numerical solution of polynomial and transcendental equations, systems of linear equations and initial value problems for ordinary differential equations. Emphasis on methods and their computational properties rather than their analytic aspects. Intended primarily for students in the physical and engineering sciences.
courses.prerequisite_text: 1 course with a minimum grade of C- from (MATH240, MATH341, MATH461, ENEE290, MATH243); and 1 course with a minimum grade of C- from (MATH241, MATH340); and 1 course with a minimum grade of C- from (CMSC106, CMSC131); and 1 course with a minimum grade of C- from (MATH246, MATH341, ENEE290, MATH243).

courses.name: Introduction to Numerical Analysis I
courses.description: Floating point computations, direct methods for linear systems, interpolation, solution of nonlinear equations.
courses.prerequisite_text: 1 course with a minimum grade of C- from (CMSC106, CMSC131); and minimum grade of C- in MATH410.

courses.name: Scientific Computing I
courses.description: Fundamental techniques in scientific computation with an introduction to theory and software for each topic. Computer numbers and sources of errors, numerical linear algebra, optimization, and Monte Carlo methods.
courses.prerequisite_text: Must have knowledge of Matlab or Python.

courses.name: Partial Differential Equations I
courses.description: Analysis of boundary value problems for Laplace's equation, initial value problems for the heat and wave equations. Fundamental solutions, maximum principles, energy methods. First order nonlinear PDE, conservation laws. Characteristics, shock formation, weak solutions. Distributions, Fourier transform.
courses.additional_info: Offered fall only. Cross-listed with MATH673.

courses.name: Research Interactions in Applied Mathematics and Scientific Computation
Advanced Topics in Applied Mathematics; The Mathematics of Quantum Information Science
Numerical Methods for Evolution Partial Differential Equations
courses.description: Topics include: Heat and wave equations: maximum principle, energy methods and Sobolev spaces, finite difference and finite element methods, von Neumann analysis, stability and error estimates;Linear first order PDEs: upwinding and monotone schemes, finite difference, finite volume, and discontinuous Galerkin methods; Nonlinear conservation laws: weak solutions and entropy conditions,monotone methods.

courses.name: Applied Statistics Practicum
courses.description: A semester-long applied statistical project (a minimum 10 hours per week or 120 hours in total), in an internship or collaborative research-laboratory setting working on a substantive applied quantitative project with significant statistical content. One option for the collaborative project is training in statistical consulting, with activities consisting of training and role-playing sessions with the Course Instructor coupled with actual non-paid short-term consulting sessions with campus graduate student and faculty clients about statistical aspects of their research.
courses.prerequisite_text: Must have completed one year of graduate study in Applied Statistics.
restrictions: Must have approved AMSC760 project proposal.

courses.name: Data Analysis Project
courses.description: This course cannot be used to meet any of the Applied Statistics Area's seminar requirements. Offered yearly, required of and limited to MS non-thesis and doctoral students in Applied Statistics Area, for whom the resulting projects serve as a Qualifying Exam component. After 5-6 lectures or presentations on components of successful data analyses and write-ups, 3-4 sessions will discuss previous student project submissions. The culminating project, to be completed in a two week period between semesters, is an analysis and written report of one of three project choices made available each year to represent a spectrum of realistic applied statistical problems.
restrictions: Permission of CMNS-Applied Mathematics department; and permission of instructor.

courses.name: Advanced Linear Numerical Analysis
courses.description: Advanced topics in numerical linear algebra, such as dense eigenvalue problems, sparse elimination, iterative methods, and other topics.
courses.prerequisite_text: AMSC666 or CMSC666; or permission of instructor.
